subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Programmable Matter: The Shape of Things to Come
description: A short lesson to help you apply Programmable Matter: The Shape of Things to Come.

hook.text: Imagine a phone that unfolds into a tablet, then refolds into a watch. Programmable matter could change shape on command.

buildup.text: Claytronics is a concept where millions of tiny robots — catoms — rearrange themselves into any physical shape.

discovery.text: Each catom would communicate with its neighbors, computing its position in the larger structure. The swarm becomes the object.

twist.text: Current catom prototypes are centimeters wide. Useful programmable matter needs sub-millimeter scale — that's decades away.

climax.text: Simpler versions exist today. Soft robots with shape-changing materials squeeze through gaps and reform. Progress is incremental.

punchline.text: A million tiny robots. One object. Any shape you want. Someday.

quiz.question: What are catoms in the context of programmable matter?
options: Atoms that have been modified at the quantum level to change bonding behavior
Tiny robots that rearrange themselves into any physical shape by communicating with neighbors
Carbon-based molecules designed to polymerize into different structures on demand
